method: Evidence gathered on 2026-10-11 with domain-restricted web searches (one domain per query, so each statement is attributable to one publisher); direct page access was blocked by the research environment's network policy, so excerpts come from the search tool's text about those pages, not from the pages themselves. Every source and claim was re-checked by an independent verifier with its own searches; only sources whose URL the verifier's search returned and claims the verifier found and judged supported are kept. Mislabelled source types were downgraded to community.

pipeline.notes: Swell direction is well corroborated by 5 publishers: Wikipedia says N/NW, Surf-Forecast WNW, SURFER W-NW, WSL NW. All fit the profile optimum of 295-320. Two sources say north swells bring sand onto the reef and cause close-outs (Wikipedia recorded; WSL/Inertia sand claims omitted because the page could not be identified). Wind: SE offshore from Surf-Forecast only. Tide 'all stages' comes from Surf-Forecast's separate Banzai Pipeline and Backdoor listing only. Period: only qualitative ('mostly groundswells'), no numeric support for 11/15 s. Size: no source gives a size range. SURFER and Surfertoday say Second Reef starts breaking at about 10-12 ft (SURFER's unattributed text adds Third Reef at about 25 ft), so the profile max of 15 ft face may be low for the outer reefs. Seasonality: Surf-Forecast says winter/January. A Wikipedia result said 'October through March', but it was hedged as 'one source' and not recorded. A WSL generated surf-report page (gamev2) said Nov-Feb and was ignored. CONFLICT on reef composition: Surfertoday's reef article says limestone plateau ('not lava'), while another Surfertoday article (page unidentified), WannaSurf and SURFER say lava reef. No peer-reviewed or measured bathymetry specific to Pipeline was found (ResearchGate/ScienceDirect searches returned nothing Pipeline-specific; a 2007 CHARTS lidar survey of Oahu's north shore was mentioned but not tied to the spot). Stormrider returned only a generic North Shore page.

mavericks.notes: Best-documented bathymetry of the five spots: a NOAA 2007 multibeam survey (rocky reef shallower than the surrounding rock, ridge promontory focusing energy) and the USGS California State Waters Map Series OFR 2014-1214 (bedrock reef; folded and faulted Purisima Formation). USGS DS 684 2 m DEMs, which include a USACE Pillar Point Harbor survey, also cover the area but were not described as Mavericks-specific. Swell direction: W-NW is consistent (SURFER 270-310, Surf-Forecast WNW, Surfertoday NW/W) and fits the 280-305 optimum. Wind: E offshore (Surf-Forecast, Surfertoday) matches 90. CONFLICT on tide: the profile says 'mid', Surfertoday says it works on all tides, and no source supports mid tide. A SURFER anecdote said lower tides made the left more approachable (not recorded as a rule). Period: long-period (USGS) and groundswell (Surfertoday), with no numeric values. Size: 25 to over 60 ft (Wikipedia), and the contest needed 30-40 ft swells (Visit Half Moon Bay), so the profile max of 50 may be low. Two NOAA pages gave 50 ft vs 60 ft maximums; the pages could not be told apart, so not recorded. Season: Nov-Mar (Visit Half Moon Bay), winter/January (Surf-Forecast). Consistency: Surf-Forecast says 'fairly consistent', while Visit Half Moon Bay says only a few ideal days per winter. No peer-reviewed wave-transformation study of Mavericks was found (only a psychology paper mentioning a 'deep reef'). The Stormrider break page exists but the result text had no conditions. WSL results were mostly generated surf-report pages and were omitted. WannaSurf returned only an anecdotal comment thread.

teahupoo.notes: Four publishers: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, WSL (two posts) and Surfer Today. They agree well. Swell direction: S to SW (Surf-Forecast says S is best; WSL gives a 180-220 window, Surfer Today SSW), all consistent with the profile's 190-225. Swell period: WSL gives 14-18 s and says short-period SSE wind swell focuses higher up the reef, consistent with the profile's 13/16 s. Wind: N to NE (Surf-Forecast NNE, Surfer Today northern breeze, WSL N/E/ESE, with SE trades still clean), consistent with the profile's 30. Tide: all tides (Surf-Forecast; WSL says mid is preferred but it works on all tides); the reef nearly dries at low tide, which is about danger, not a preference. Season: Surfer Today says April-September, matching the profile; Surf-Forecast says autumn, most often April. Size: WSL gives 4-12 ft for best conditions, and a WSL piece says it holds up to 20-25 ft. The WSL summary merged three posts (What Makes Teahupo'o Tick, Break Breakdown: Tackling Tubes, Teahupo'o Essentials). Claims are split between the two posts that most likely hold them; publisher-level attribution is reliable, page-level is approximate. The Surfer Today claims come from several of its Teahupoo articles and are filed under the first-ranked one. Peer-reviewed gap: the ResearchGate search summary described a lab physical model reproducing the Teahupo'o reef bathymetry (steep forereef, about 1:2.29) used to test the SWASH model. It could not be tied to a specific returned link (none of the titles named Teahupo'o), so it was not cited; worth a targeted follow-up. No measured survey data was found.

supertubos.notes: Four publishers found: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, the WSL (official) and WannaSurf. ResearchGate and ScienceDirect searches found no peer-reviewed study of Supertubos itself, only general sandbar/refraction work and Nazaré canyon geology. Swell direction agrees across sources: SW, SW-W, and NW/W/SW; WannaSurf's NW sits about 5 deg outside the profile window. Size agrees: head-high to double-overhead (WSL) and 1-1.5 m holding 3 m+ (WannaSurf). TIDE CONFLICT: WannaSurf and a WSL guide both prefer mid to high tide, and the WSL results also say low tide can close the break out (not recorded as a claim because the page could not be identified). The profile says low_to_mid. Wind: NE (Surf-Forecast) and N (WSL/Nic von Rupp) agree with the profile's 40; WannaSurf's N/NW does not. Bathymetry: a sandbar/sand bottom (WannaSurf, WSL), though Surf-Forecast calls it 'beach and reef'. Von Rupp says an offshore canyon refracts swell, and that the spot is somewhat sheltered and needs big swells. Seasonality: only indirect evidence (Surf-Forecast: summer mostly flat), consistent with the profile's Sep-Mar. Page-level attribution caveat: the WSL summary blended several posts. The size/direction guide is assigned to 'Break Breakdown: How to Place in Peniche with Pires'. The mid-to-high tide and 'pumping sandbar' lines are assigned to the event guide but may come from another WSL post; the publisher is the same either way.

Tide conflict: the WSL break breakdown says any tide at La Graviere (low to mid for Hossegor in general), against the profile's mid. Surf-forecast gives no tide preference. thurso-east.notes: The sources agree well with the profile. Swell direction: Surf-Forecast gives NNW and SurferToday gives NW/N/WNW, both inside the 300-345 optimum and the 280-30 window. Tide: Surf-Forecast says mid and rising; SurferToday says medium to high. The profile's 'mid' is consistent. Size: Wikipedia and SurferToday's table give 2-15 ft, but SurferToday's prose says 10-20 ft (an internal discrepancy). Season: SurferToday gives Sep-May; Surf-Forecast says it can work at any time of year (not recorded, since it is not a best-season claim). Period: Surf-Forecast says most surf is groundswell; no source gives numbers for the 11/15 s profile. Surf-Forecast classifies it as an exposed point break. The VisitScotland results were not spot-specific (operator promotion and an event listing), so nothing was recorded. No peer-reviewed or bathymetric survey was found.

raglan-manu-bay.notes: TIDE CONFLICT with the profile: Surf-Forecast says best around low tide and WannaSurf says low and mid. Consider changing the profile from 'mid' to 'low_to_mid'. WannaSurf also says it is more hollow at low tide. SWELL DIRECTION CONFLICT between sources: Surf-Forecast says SW/WSW (agrees with 220-260), while WannaSurf says NW and W (marked as disagreeing). The WannaSurf summary also mentions a Raglan regional note favouring a S/SW groundswell. Wind: Surf-Forecast SE and WannaSurf SW/S/SE are both consistent with 140. Size: Wikipedia 2-10+ ft, WannaSurf 3-16 ft, WSL best contest days 4-5 ft. These overlap the profile's 3-12. Season: Surf-Forecast says winter (June) and WSL scheduled its CT for May as the 'optimal time of year'. Both fall within the profile's Mar-Oct. Period: Surf-Forecast says mostly groundswell; no numbers. Bathymetry: a ResearchGate figure caption (after Scarfe 2002a) describes large-scale and small-scale wedges plus a ridge; WannaSurf says boulders. The search also surfaced text saying Scarfe et al. (2002) classified Manu Bay as a macro wedge plus meso wedge with a superimposed ridge forming 'The Ledge'. This was not recorded because the summary did not say which ResearchGate page it came from. The source_type of the ResearchGate figure is marked peer_reviewed, but the host publication's venue was not shown. Wikipedia page-level attribution (Raglan vs Surfing in New Zealand article) is inferred. newzealand.com called Manu Bay 'widely described as the world's longest left'; this was not recorded because it is hedged and promotional.

mullaghmore-head.notes: surf-forecast.com's 'Mullaghmore' page (https://www.surf-forecast.com/breaks/Mullaghmore) describes a SHELTERED BEACH BREAK (all tides, NW swell, SE offshore). It is a different break from the Mullaghmore Head reef, so it was excluded. Swell direction: SurferToday W-NW and WannaSurf NW and W agree with 285-320. Wind: only WannaSurf states directions (SE, E, NE; centred on E, 45 deg from the profile's 135, borderline). SurferToday only says 'light offshore', so it was not recorded. No source explicitly confirms SE. Tide: SurferToday says high only; WannaSurf says mid and high. Both are consistent with mid_to_high. Size: WannaSurf says it starts at 12 ft+ and holds 16 ft and over. Recorded big days were 49 ft (Wikipedia, March 2012) and 60 ft (Wikipedia and SurferToday, Oct 2020 Hurricane Epsilon), which slightly exceed the profile's 50 ft max. Discover Ireland pages give a range of 30-50 ft. Season: SurferToday gives Oct-Mar, matching exactly. Period: no source states a period, so the 14/17 s profile values are unverified. Discover Ireland claims came from several returned pages; they are attributed to the Mullaghmore Head page, which is the most likely match, but page-level attribution is uncertain. Wikipedia page-level attribution (Surfing in Ireland table vs Mullaghmore, County Sligo article) is inferred. Location: about 400 m NW of Mullaghmore village (Wikipedia, SurferToday). No peer-reviewed or survey bathymetry was found within the budget.
